chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: Leaving the band to job around Chicago
summary: With a new ballroom drawing the money, he quits and earns more on jobbing dates, meeting pianist George Zack and other jazz players.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yes but then Bill got on the booze - so - and of course, Eddie was serious with those guys and there was a new ballroom down on Wilson Avenue - on the beach - they had built one and Eddie went in there and all of a sudden, the money started coming down. And, so, I decided I'd get the hell out of that band because it wasn't working enough, you know. And, I liked to play and, so, I got acquainted with all the guys around - you know - at that point; I got to know George Zackin---
Fine piano player - he lives in Tucson now - doesn't he?
Yeah - I guess so. But, all the good players - the jazz players that were around - I got in with them and they were having me on their jobing dates - you know and that's how I met all these guys.
And, so, you started doing pretty well just on your own jobing - right?

Doing better financially really than staying with the band, because I was doing some big jobs - you know - big party jobs and doing some -- even playing big picnics and getting a lot of money for that.
